Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Education | National Don’t punish BECE candidates for GES failures – Adutwum’s spokesperson tells Education Minister Source : Myjoyonline.com 24 November 2026 7:12pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The spokesperson for former Education Minister Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum has criticised a directive by the current Education Minister, Haruna Iddrisu, concerning BECE candidates, arguing that learners should not be penalised for administrative failures within the Ghana Education Service (GES).
In a statement, Yaw Opoku Mensah described the directive as “misplaced, unjustifiable, and deeply misguided”, insisting that the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) registration process is managed by GES and not individual candidates.
He said the examination was administered by the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) based on submissions processed through the GES administrative structure, making the service responsible for any irregularities in the registration process.
According to him, headteachers register candidates electronically in line with WAEC's requirements before forwarding the information to District Examination Officers for processing and verification through the Student CASS Portal.
He explained that an Entry Report is generated to allow for corrections before the final submission to WAEC within the stipulated October/November registration period.
“Every stage of this process falls within the administrative responsibility of GES, under the supervision of the Deputy Director-General responsible for Quality and Access, whose portfolio encompasses Schools and Instruction,” he said.
Mr Mensah maintained that candidates do not independently register for the examination and should therefore not be held responsible for errors or omissions arising from the administrative process.
He questioned why learners whose details had been verified and processed through an official government system should suffer the consequences of failures they had no control over.
“So, how does a Minister arrive at the absurd conclusion that learners whose details were verified, registered, and processed through an official government administrative system should suffer the consequences of an institutional failure they neither caused nor had the authority to prevent?” he asked.
He called on the government to investigate any breaches in the registration process and hold the officials responsible accountable instead of imposing sanctions on candidates.
“If GES submitted the names, then GES must answer for the integrity of those submissions. If there were procedural breaches, investigate them. If officials failed to discharge their responsibilities, sanction them. But do not sacrifice the academic future of innocent children to conceal or compensate for institutional incompetence,” he said.
The spokesperson also raised concerns about what he described as the apparent abandonment or scaling down of the Ghana Education Service Management Information System (GESMIS), which he said was introduced under the previous administration to improve the management of educational data.
He said the system was designed to support administrative decision-making, institutional planning, operational efficiency and accountability within GES.
Mr Mensah questioned why the current administration had not strengthened and expanded the digital infrastructure, arguing that weakening such systems could contribute to administrative challenges.
“If the current leadership has deliberately weakened or abandoned systems capable of improving efficiency, transparency, and accountability, it cannot escape responsibility for the administrative consequences,” he said.
He urged the Education Minister to hold GES leadership accountable for any failures in the registration process, stressing that learners had no role in managing the registration portal or supervising examination entries.
“The children are not the administrators. They are not the District Examination Officers. They do not manage the registration portal, and they certainly do not supervise the examination registration process,” he said.
He added that the academic future of learners should not be jeopardised by administrative negligence or institutional failures.
